# Where does FHIR fit in your research?

[Learn how FHIR can help you access electronic health record data, bring new tools into clinical workflows, and make research data easier to reuse.]{.home-lead}

HL7® FHIR® (Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources, pronounced “fire”) is a standard for representing and exchanging health data. It also provides ways to implement [common data elements](https://datascience.nih.gov/fhir-initiatives/common-data-elements) and standardize their terminology. These capabilities can support [FAIR data practices](https://datascience.nih.gov/data-ecosystem): making data findable, accessible, interoperable, and reusable.

This guide explains the concepts and technologies, with examples and workshops to help you apply them in your own work.

::: home-actions
[Start with the FHIR introduction →](sections/introduction.qmd){.home-button .home-button-primary}
:::
::::

:::::: {.home-research-map aria-label="Three ways FHIR can support research"}
## What can FHIR do to support research? {.home-map-title}

::: home-map-step

### Bring research innovations into clinical workflows

Use [SMART on FHIR](modules/smart-on-fhir-intro.qmd) to integrate research apps with EHRs, [CDS Hooks](modules/cds-hooks-intro.qmd) to deliver clinical decision support during care, and [Clinical Quality Language (CQL)](modules/clinical-quality-language-intro.qmd) to express the underlying logic.
:::

::: home-map-step

### Automate EHR data collection

Pull available clinical data directly from EHRs into [REDCap](modules/redcap-fhir.qmd) using FHIR, reducing manual data entry for chart abstraction.
:::

::: home-map-step

### Access data for a study population

[FHIR Bulk Data](modules/bulk-fhir-intro.qmd) lets you retrieve data for a patient population in a consistent, structured format.
:::

## Find tools for your research

Learn how FHIR and related technologies can help you access EHR data, specify study data requirements, and build and test applications.

::::::::: home-technology-grid
::: home-technology
### Define your data requirements

Read and write **FHIR Implementation Guides** that specify data structures and terminology for a particular use case.

[Explore Implementation Guides →](sections/technologies.qmd#fhir-implementation-guides){.home-text-link}
:::

::: home-technology
### Connect applications to EHRs

Learn how to use **SMART on FHIR** to launch an app from an EHR and request access to the data it needs.

[Explore SMART on FHIR →](sections/technologies.qmd#smart-on-fhir){.home-text-link}
:::

::: home-technology
### Access population-scale data

Use **FHIR Bulk Data** to export records for a study population, with examples covering authorization, data retrieval, and preparation for analysis.

[Explore FHIR Bulk Data →](sections/technologies.qmd#fhir-bulk-data){.home-text-link}
:::

::: home-technology
### Add clinical decision support

Learn how **CDS Hooks** connects decision support to events in clinical care and how **Clinical Quality Language (CQL)** represents the logic behind recommendations.

[Explore CDS Hooks →](sections/technologies.qmd#cds-hooks){.home-text-link} [Explore CQL →](sections/technologies.qmd#clinical-quality-language){.home-text-link}
:::

::: home-technology
### Bring EHR data into REDCap

Learn how **REDCap** uses FHIR to import clinical data into research projects, and what your team needs to set up the integration.

[Explore REDCap and FHIR →](sections/technologies.qmd#redcap){.home-text-link}
:::

::: home-technology
### Test with synthetic patient data

Generate synthetic patient records with **Synthea™**, then customize the data for testing FHIR applications and analysis workflows.

[Explore Synthea →](sections/technologies.qmd#synthea){.home-text-link}
:::
